The bug is in the `_eval_col_insert` method. The last return statement has:
```python
return self[i, j - pos - other.cols]
```

But it should be:
```python
return self[i, j - other.cols]
```

Because when `j >= pos + other.cols`, the column in the original matrix should be `j - other.cols` (since we've inserted `other.cols` columns).

Found the bug. In `_eval_col_insert` in `sympy/matrices/common.py`, line 91:

```python
return self[i, j - pos - other.cols]
```

should be:

```python
return self[i, j - other.cols]
```

When `j >= pos + other.cols`, we need to map back to the original matrix column index by subtracting only the number of inserted columns (`other.cols`), not `pos + other.cols`.
